newsitem.title: FINLAND: OKOB SEES WEAKER END-YEAR BUT 1996 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: OKOB SEES WEAKER END-YEAR BUT 1996 PROFIT.

text.p: Osuuspankkien Keskuspankki Oy (OKOBANK) -- the central bank for Finland's cooperative banks -- said in a statement on Monday the end-year trend would be weaker but it still expected to post a full-year 1996 profit.

"The earnings trend towards the end of the year is forecasted to be weaker than in the period from January to September. The net operating result of the whole year is, nevertheless, estimated to be clearly in the black and substantially better than last year," OKOBANK said in its nine-month interim report.
In 1995, OKOBANK posted a 47 million markka net operating loss after credit losses.
In January-September, the bank jumped to a 248 million markka operating profit from a 32 million markka loss.

Referring to the nine-month figure, OKOBANK said: "The better than expected performance was mainly due to the fact that the net operating profit figure contained significant non-recurring gains on the sale of assets, commission and fee income as well as income attributable to the changes in valuation and booking principles."
At 359 million markka in January-September, OKOBANK's net income from financial operations was 42 million markka lower than in the year-ago period.

But taking into account that price differences in the bank's bond portfolio were not periodised in last year's nine-month accounts, "the comparable net income from financial operations was nearly as large as it was a year ago", OKOBANK said.

Net income from securities transactions rose to 211 million markka from 64 million, and commission income rose by 67 million markka to 299 million "due to the exceptionally large commission income on securities transactions," it said.
Net income from securities transactions included a 61 million markka gain from OKOBANK's sale of Tuko Oy shares, the bank said.

Net loan and guarantee losses and write-downs fell to 203 million markka from 267 million. The bank's non-performing claims were 345 million markka at end-Septeber, down by 366 million compared to the same time one year earlier. OKOBANK's zero-interest claims at 221 million markka were 309 million less than at end-September 1995.
